title: Properties of Quadrilaterals: Sides, Angles and Diagonals
seo_title: Year 8 Quadrilaterals Worksheets: Properties, Angles and Diagonals (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: establish properties of quadrilaterals using congruent triangles and angle properties, and solve related problems explaining reasoning
meta_desc: Free Year 8 maths worksheets on quadrilaterals for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M8SP02): parallelograms, rectangles, rhombuses, squares, kites and trapeziums, their angles and diagonals, and reasoning with congruent triangles. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Parallelogram diagonals bisect each other. Rectangle diagonals are equal. Rhombus and kite diagonals meet at right angles.
key_sub: The angles in a quadrilateral add to 360°. A square is both a rectangle and a rhombus.
body_html:
How it works

  • Parallelogram: opposite sides parallel and equal; opposite angles equal; diagonals bisect each other.
  • Rectangle: a parallelogram with four right angles; diagonals are equal.
  • Rhombus: a parallelogram with four equal sides; diagonals meet at right angles and bisect the angles.
  • Square: both a rectangle and a rhombus.
  • Kite: two pairs of equal adjacent sides; diagonals meet at right angles; one pair of opposite angles equal.
  • Trapezium: exactly one pair of parallel sides; co-interior angles add to 180°.

The angles in any quadrilateral add to 360°. Many properties can be proved by drawing a diagonal and using congruent triangles.

Example

In parallelogram ABCD, angle A = 65°. Find angles B, C and D.

B is co-interior with A: 180° − 65° = 115°.

Opposite angles are equal.

Answer: B = 115°, C = 65°, D = 115°

Example

The diagonals of a rhombus are 6 cm and 8 cm. Find the side length.

Half-diagonals are 3 cm and 4 cm and meet at 90°.

√(3² + 4²) = 5.

Answer: 5 cm

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a square is not a rectangle. A square has four right angles, so it is a special rectangle.
  • Mixing up diagonals: a rectangle's are equal; a rhombus's meet at right angles.
  • Taking co-interior angles as equal. They add to 180°.
  • Using 180° as the angle sum of a quadrilateral. It is 360°.

faq.q: What are the properties of a parallelogram?
faq.a: Opposite sides are parallel and equal, opposite angles are equal, neighbouring angles add to 180° and the diagonals bisect each other.

faq.q: What is the difference between a rhombus and a square?
faq.a: Both have four equal sides, but a square also has four right angles and equal diagonals.
Yes. A rectangle is a quadrilateral with four right angles, and a square has four right angles.

faq.q: How do congruent triangles prove properties of quadrilaterals?
faq.a: Drawing a diagonal splits the shape into two triangles. If they are congruent (for example by SSS), their matching sides and angles are equal.

items.q: Is every rectangle a square?
c: Yes, both have four right angles
No, its sides need not all be equal
items.e: A 3 cm by 5 cm rectangle is not a square, so no.

items.q: Which quadrilateral has both a rectangle's and a rhombus's properties?
items.e: Four right angles and four equal sides: a square.

items.q: A quadrilateral has diagonals that are equal in length and bisect each other, but do not meet at right angles. What is it?
items.e: A quadrilateral that has diagonals that are equal in length and bisect each other, but do not meet at right angles is a rectangle.

items.q: A quadrilateral has four equal sides and four right angles. What is it?
items.e: A quadrilateral that has four equal sides and four right angles is a square.

items.q: Is every rhombus a parallelogram?
c: Yes, both pairs of opposite sides are parallel
No, a rhombus is a kite
No, a rhombus has equal sides
Only if it has right angles
items.e: A rhombus has two pairs of parallel sides, so yes.

items.q: A quadrilateral has four equal sides, but its angles are not right angles. What is it?
items.e: A quadrilateral that has four equal sides, but its angles are not right angles is a rhombus.

items.q: A quadrilateral has one pair of parallel sides and its two non-parallel sides are equal. What is it?
items.e: A quadrilateral that has one pair of parallel sides and its two non-parallel sides are equal is a isosceles trapezium.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rhombus (that is not a square) have?
items.e: Its two diagonals are lines of symmetry: 2.

items.q: A quadrilateral has one diagonal that cuts the other in half at right angles, but not the other way round. What is it?
items.e: A quadrilateral that has one diagonal that cuts the other in half at right angles, but not the other way round is a kite.

items.q: A quadrilateral has two pairs of parallel sides, but no right angles and not all sides equal. What is it?
items.e: A quadrilateral that has two pairs of parallel sides, but no right angles and not all sides equal is a parallelogram.

items.q: Is a rhombus a special kind of kite?
c: Only if it is a square
No, a kite has no parallel sides
Yes, it has two pairs of equal adjacent sides
No, a kite has no equal sides
items.e: All four sides of a rhombus are equal, so it has two pairs of equal adjacent sides: yes.

items.q: A quadrilateral has two pairs of equal adjacent sides and its diagonals meet at right angles. What is it?
items.e: A quadrilateral that has two pairs of equal adjacent sides and its diagonals meet at right angles is a kite.

items.q: Is every square a rectangle?
c: No, a rectangle has two long sides
No, because its sides are all equal
Yes, because it has four right angles
items.e: A rectangle needs four right angles. A square has them, so every square is a rectangle.

items.q: A quadrilateral has diagonals that are equal in length and bisect each other at right angles. What is it?
items.e: A quadrilateral that has diagonals that are equal in length and bisect each other at right angles is a square.

items.q: A quadrilateral has diagonals that bisect each other at right angles but are not equal. What is it?
items.e: A quadrilateral that has diagonals that bisect each other at right angles but are not equal is a rhombus.

items.q: Is every square a rhombus?
c: No, a square is a rectangle
No, a rhombus has no right angles
Yes, it has four equal sides
items.e: A rhombus needs four equal sides. A square has them, so yes.

items.q: A quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides. What is it?
items.e: A quadrilateral that has exactly one pair of parallel sides is a trapezium.

items.q: Which of these is NOT always a parallelogram?
items.e: A trapezium has only one pair of parallel sides: trapezium.

items.q: A quadrilateral has four right angles, but its sides are not all equal. What is it?
items.e: A quadrilateral that has four right angles, but its sides are not all equal is a rectangle.

items.q: A quadrilateral has diagonals that bisect each other but are not equal and do not meet at right angles. What is it?
items.e: A quadrilateral that has diagonals that bisect each other but are not equal and do not meet at right angles is a parallelogram.

items.q: Which property does every parallelogram have?
items.e: In a parallelogram opposite angles are equal and opposite sides are equal and parallel.

items.q: Which property does every rectangle have?
c: The diagonals are equal in length
Exactly one pair of parallel sides
The diagonals meet at right angles
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other.

items.q: Which property does every rhombus have?
c: The diagonals meet at right angles
Only one pair of parallel sides
items.e: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles.

items.q: Which property does every kite have?
c: One pair of opposite angles is equal
Both pairs of opposite angles are equal
items.e: The angles between the unequal sides of a kite are equal: one pair of opposite angles.

items.q: Which property does every square have that a rhombus may not?
items.e: Both have equal sides and perpendicular diagonals, but only a square must have equal diagonals.

items.q: Which property does every rectangle have that a parallelogram may not?
items.e: Every parallelogram has the other three; a rectangle also has four right angles.

items.q: The diagonals of a parallelogram…
items.e: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other (cut each other in half).

items.q: Which quadrilateral can have exactly one line of symmetry?
items.e: A kite has one line of symmetry along its main diagonal.

items.q: Which quadrilateral has rotational symmetry of order 2 but no lines of symmetry (in general)?
items.e: A general parallelogram looks the same after a half turn but has no mirror lines.

items.q: Co-interior angles in a trapezium (between the parallel sides) add up to…
items.e: Co-interior angles between parallel lines are supplementary: 180°.

items.q: The angles in any quadrilateral add up to…
items.e: A diagonal splits a quadrilateral into two triangles: 2 × 180° = 360°.

items.q: In an isosceles trapezium, the two angles at the longer parallel side are…
items.e: An isosceles trapezium is symmetric, so its base angles are equal.

items.q: Which statement about a square is FALSE?
c: Its diagonals are longer than its sides by 1 cm
items.e: The diagonal of a square is about 1.41 times the side, not 1 cm longer. The others are all true.

items.q: Which statement about a rhombus is TRUE?
c: It has only one pair of parallel sides
items.e: Each diagonal of a rhombus cuts the angles at its ends in half: its diagonals bisect its angles.

items.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does a kite have (that is not a rhombus)?
items.e: A kite has no parallel sides unless it is a rhombus.

items.q: Which quadrilateral has diagonals that are equal but do not bisect each other?
items.e: The diagonals of an isosceles trapezium are equal, but they do not cut each other in half.

items.q: Which two quadrilaterals have diagonals that meet at right angles?
items.e: The diagonals of a rhombus and a kite are perpendicular (and so are a square's).

items.q: A parallelogram has one right angle. What can you say about it?
items.e: Opposite angles are equal and co-interior angles add to 180°, so all four are 90°: a rectangle.

items.q: A parallelogram has two adjacent sides equal. What can you say about it?
items.e: Opposite sides are equal too, so all four sides are equal: a rhombus.

items.q: Which shape's diagonals divide it into four congruent triangles?
items.e: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles, making four congruent right-angled triangles.

items.q: In parallelogram ABCD, angle A = 97°. What is angle B?
items.e: Angles A and B are co-interior, so they add to 180°: 180° − 97° = 83°.

items.q: A kite has angles of 65° and 117° at the ends of its line of symmetry. The other two angles are equal. Find one of them.
An isosceles trapezium has two angles of 52° at its longer parallel side. What is each of the other two angles?
items.e: Each pair of co-interior angles adds to 180°: 180° − 52° = 128°.

items.q: In parallelogram ABCD, angle A = 72°. What is angle C?
items.e: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal: 72°.

items.q: A kite has angles of 129° and 71° at the ends of its line of symmetry. The other two angles are equal. Find one of them.
In parallelogram ABCD, angle A = 131°. What is angle B?
items.e: Angles A and B are co-interior, so they add to 180°: 180° − 131° = 49°.

items.q: An isosceles trapezium has two angles of 66° at its longer parallel side. What is each of the other two angles?
items.e: Each pair of co-interior angles adds to 180°: 180° − 66° = 114°.

items.q: In trapezium ABCD, AB is parallel to DC and angle A = 124°. What is angle D?
items.e: Angles A and D are co-interior between parallel lines, so they add to 180°: 56°.

items.q: An isosceles trapezium has two angles of 72° at its longer parallel side. What is each of the other two angles?
items.e: Each pair of co-interior angles adds to 180°: 180° − 72° = 108°.

items.q: In parallelogram ABCD, angle A = 83°. What is angle B?
items.e: Angles A and B are co-interior, so they add to 180°: 180° − 83° = 97°.

items.q: In parallelogram ABCD, angle A = 92°. What is angle B?
items.e: Angles A and B are co-interior, so they add to 180°: 180° − 92° = 88°.

items.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 127°, 124° and 71°. What is the fourth angle?
A kite has angles of 73° and 105° at the ends of its line of symmetry. The other two angles are equal. Find one of them.
Three angles of a quadrilateral are 81°, 79° and 117°. What is the fourth angle?
An isosceles trapezium has two angles of 68° at its longer parallel side. What is each of the other two angles?
items.e: Each pair of co-interior angles adds to 180°: 180° − 68° = 112°.

items.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 106°, 99° and 86°. What is the fourth angle?
An isosceles trapezium has two angles of 83° at its longer parallel side. What is each of the other two angles?
items.e: Each pair of co-interior angles adds to 180°: 180° − 83° = 97°.

items.q: An isosceles trapezium has two angles of 56° at its longer parallel side. What is each of the other two angles?
items.e: Each pair of co-interior angles adds to 180°: 180° − 56° = 124°.

items.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 72°, 119° and 81°. What is the fourth angle?
An isosceles trapezium has two angles of 73° at its longer parallel side. What is each of the other two angles?
items.e: Each pair of co-interior angles adds to 180°: 180° − 73° = 107°.

items.q: The diagonals of parallelogram PQRS meet at M. PM = 4x + 4 and MR = 2x + 8. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other, so PM = MR: 4x + 4 = 2x + 8. So 2x = 4 and x = 2.

items.q: The diagonals of a rhombus are 24 cm and 32 cm long. How long is each side?
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, making right-angled triangles with legs 12 cm and 16 cm. Side = √(12² + 16²) = 20 cm.

items.q: The diagonals of parallelogram PQRS meet at M. PM = 2x + 5 and MR = x + 9. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other, so PM = MR: 2x + 5 = x + 9. So x = 4 and x = 4.

items.q: The diagonals of a rhombus are 10 cm and 24 cm long. How long is each side?
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, making right-angled triangles with legs 5 cm and 12 cm. Side = √(5² + 12²) = 13 cm.

items.q: The diagonals of a rhombus are 16 cm and 30 cm long. How long is each side?
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, making right-angled triangles with legs 8 cm and 15 cm. Side = √(8² + 15²) = 17 cm.

items.q: In rectangle ABCD, AC = 3x + 5 and BD = 23 cm. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal: 3x + 5 = 23, so 3x = 18 and x = 6.

items.q: The diagonals of parallelogram PQRS meet at M. PM = 3x + 5 and MR = 2x + 12. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other, so PM = MR: 3x + 5 = 2x + 12. So x = 7 and x = 7.

items.q: The diagonals of rectangle ABCD meet at E. AC = 42 cm. How long is BE?
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other, so BE = ½ × 42 = 21 cm.

items.q: The diagonals of a rhombus are 6 cm and 8 cm long. How long is each side?
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, making right-angled triangles with legs 3 cm and 4 cm. Side = √(3² + 4²) = 5 cm.

items.q: The diagonals of rectangle ABCD meet at E. AC = 54 cm. How long is BE?
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other, so BE = ½ × 54 = 27 cm.

items.q: The diagonals of rectangle ABCD meet at E. AC = 28 cm. How long is BE?
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other, so BE = ½ × 28 = 14 cm.

items.q: The diagonals of rectangle ABCD meet at E. AC = 44 cm. How long is BE?
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other, so BE = ½ × 44 = 22 cm.

items.q: The diagonals of rectangle ABCD meet at E. AC = 20 cm. How long is BE?
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other, so BE = ½ × 20 = 10 cm.

items.q: In rectangle ABCD, AC = 4x + 4 and BD = 24 cm. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal: 4x + 4 = 24, so 4x = 20 and x = 5.

items.q: The diagonals of a rhombus are 12 cm and 16 cm long. How long is each side?
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, making right-angled triangles with legs 6 cm and 8 cm. Side = √(6² + 8²) = 10 cm.

items.q: In rectangle ABCD, AC = 2x + 8 and BD = 12 cm. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal: 2x + 8 = 12, so 2x = 4 and x = 2.

items.q: The diagonals of rectangle ABCD meet at E. AC = 14 cm. How long is BE?
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other, so BE = ½ × 14 = 7 cm.

items.q: In rectangle ABCD, AC = 3x + 4 and BD = 13 cm. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal: 3x + 4 = 13, so 3x = 9 and x = 3.

items.q: The diagonals of rectangle ABCD meet at E. AC = 24 cm. How long is BE?
items.e: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other, so BE = ½ × 24 = 12 cm.

items.q: The diagonals of parallelogram PQRS meet at M. PM = 2x + 5 and MR = x + 14. Find x.
items.e: The diagonals bisect each other, so PM = MR: 2x + 5 = x + 14. So x = 9 and x = 9.

items.q: A diagonal is drawn in parallelogram ABCD, from A to C. Which test shows that triangles ABC and CDA are congruent?
items.e: AB = CD and BC = DA (opposite sides), and AC is shared: SSS.

items.q: Why are the opposite angles of a parallelogram equal?
c: A diagonal splits it into two congruent triangles
It has a line of symmetry
All its angles are right angles
items.e: The diagonal makes two congruent triangles, so matching angles are equal: two congruent triangles.

items.q: In kite ABCD, AB = AD and CB = CD. Which test shows triangles ABC and ADC are congruent?
items.e: AB = AD, CB = CD and AC is shared: SSS.

items.q: A quadrilateral has angles 90°, 90°, 90° and x°. What is x?
items.e: 360 − 270 = 90, so it is a rectangle (or square).

items.q: A rhombus has one angle of 64°. What are its other three angles?
items.e: Opposite angles are equal and neighbouring angles add to 180°: 116°, 64°, 116°.

items.q: A square has a side of 6 cm. How long is its diagonal, to 1 decimal place?
A rectangle is 8 cm by 6 cm. How long is each diagonal?
A rhombus has a side of 10 cm and one diagonal of 12 cm. How long is the other diagonal?
items.e: Half-diagonals: 6 and √(10² − 6²) = 8. Other diagonal = 2 × 8 = 16 cm.

items.q: The angles of a quadrilateral are x, 2x, 3x and 4x. What is the largest angle?
In parallelogram PQRS, angle P = 3x and angle Q = 2x. Find angle P.
items.e: Co-interior: 5x = 180, so x = 36 and angle P = 108°.

items.q: Which is the best name for a quadrilateral with vertices (0, 0), (4, 0), (4, 3) and (0, 3)?
items.e: Four right angles, sides 4 and 3: rectangle.

items.q: Which is the best name for a quadrilateral with vertices (0, 0), (3, 1), (4, 4) and (1, 3)?
items.e: Every side is √10 long, but the angles are not 90° (the diagonals are different lengths): rhombus.

items.q: Amelia says a shape with four equal sides must be a square. Is she right?
c: No, it could be a trapezium
No, it could be a kite with unequal sides
No, it could be a rhombus
items.e: A rhombus has four equal sides without right angles, so no.

items.q: A kite has angles 110°, 70° and y, y, where the two y angles are equal. Find y.
The diagonals of a quadrilateral are equal and bisect each other at right angles. What is it?
items.e: Equal and bisecting → rectangle; at right angles → rhombus. Both: square.

items.q: A quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides, and its two angles at one base are 70° and 70°. What is it?
items.e: One pair of parallel sides with equal base angles: isosceles trapezium.

items.q: In rhombus ABCD, angle ABD = 35°. What is angle ABC?
items.e: The diagonal BD bisects angle B, so angle ABC = 2 × 35° = 70°.

items.q: In rectangle ABCD, the diagonals meet at E and angle AEB = 120°. What is angle EAB?
items.e: AE = BE (half-diagonals are equal), so triangle AEB is isosceles: (180° − 120°) ÷ 2 = 30°.

items.q: A trapezium has parallel sides 6 cm and 10 cm. How many pairs of equal angles must it have?
items.e: A general trapezium only has co-interior angles adding to 180°. Equal angles are only guaranteed in an isosceles trapezium: none.

items.q: Which set of conditions proves a quadrilateral is a parallelogram?
c: Both pairs of opposite sides are equal
One pair of sides is parallel
items.e: If both pairs of opposite sides are equal, a diagonal makes two congruent triangles (SSS), which makes the sides parallel: parallelogram.
